external_sources.title: Feature interaction in software product line engineering: A systematic mapping study
external_sources.fragment: Feature interaction is established prior art; interaction order can involve more than two features and exhaustive configuration grows combinatorially.
external_sources.kill: Do not claim novelty for feature-interaction detection, graphs, or the generic exponential interaction problem.

external_sources.title: Software product line testing: a systematic literature review
external_sources.fragment: Combinatorial interaction testing and runtime feature-interaction graphs are established methods; pairwise coverage is common but does not prove absence of higher-order effects.
external_sources.kill: Do not claim novelty for pairwise combinatorial coverage or feature interaction graphs.

external_sources.title: The Interaction between Inputs and Configurations fed to Software Systems: an Empirical Study
external_sources.fragment: Configuration effects can depend non-monotonically on input data; context×geometry or context×evidence terms should therefore be treated as first-class confound/interaction candidates.
external_sources.kill: Do not assume configuration effects transport independently of workload/input.

fragments.fragment: Interaction existence is generic prior art; EvoNOMOS novelty, if any, must sit in typed operational primitives, prospective freezing, exact matched interventions, and cross-domain transport.
Pairwise coverage is a search strategy, not evidence that pairwise structure is sufficient.
A higher-order term needs supported factorial cells; missing cells are underidentification, not zero coefficients.
Repository-native Boolean gates provide unusually clean natural factorial families when lifecycle, authority, geometry and command semantics are separately encoded.
Cross-domain replication should transport interaction semantics rather than syntax: Prow Go branching and Serge Actions YAML can instantiate the same authority×lifecycle×PR gate.
Configuration/input nonseparability literature supports keeping G/E controls explicit rather than treating all action reversal as X×X interaction.

An interaction hypergraph can be more scientifically useful than a single scalar law because it preserves which primitive combinations are identified, transported, one-domain-only, or underidentified.
Negative interaction findings are reusable: failure to transport a Kafka compatibility×coexistence candidate narrows the law rather than merely weakening it.

paper_seeds.working_title: From Context Primitives to Interaction Laws: Prospective Cross-Repository Reconstruction of Software Policy Gates
paper_seeds.core: P12-P17 trajectory: anti-rationalized primitive basis plus prospectively matched, cross-domain interaction transport.
paper_seeds.risk: Evidence may remain concentrated in bot/workflow decision gates; broader software-design transport is still required.

paper_seeds.working_title: Anti-Rationalization by Construction: Prospective Intervention Grammar for Repository-Native Software Design Science
paper_seeds.core: Constitution/preseal, exactness guards, negative controls, held-out repository worlds, hosted executable reconstruction.
paper_seeds.risk: Could look like workflow formalism unless tied to concrete scientific gains and falsified alternatives.

paper_seeds.working_title: Harvest Without Authority: Reusable Failure Capital and Non-Sovereign Literature Backflow in a Multi-Lab Research OS
paper_seeds.core: Source→fragment→cross-lab reuse while blocking repeated retrieval from becoming authority.
paper_seeds.risk: Needs empirical evidence of reuse and downstream benefit, not just architecture description.

cross_lab_backflow.reason: Pairwise-vs-higher-order support and failed-transport semantics map naturally onto mediation/bridge ecology.
Underidentification, representation dependence and negative result retention.
Authority×lifecycle interaction and process-gated authority semantics may donate rivals without transferring doctrine.
Higher-order structure, sparse hypergraphs and representation-specific interaction claims.
